result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers keep the body size, line-height and headline settings, add no fonts, and name specific strengths such as the measure, the label tracking and tabular-nums. A makes one well-justified edit: changing px to rem so the body text respects the user's browser font-size setting, which matters for an older patient base. Its contrast figures are also accurate (about 6:1). B makes no required changes and offers an optional text-wrap tweak, but it dismisses the px body size as a matter of taste, so it misses the one accessibility issue in the sheet. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers keep the body and headline settings, add no fonts, and point to specific strengths such as the measure, the label tracking and the tabular times. B's single change, swapping 17px for 1.0625rem, is a real accessibility fix: a px body size ignores the user's browser font-size setting, which matters for a dental practice. A waves this off as a matter of taste, which is slightly wrong. A comes closest to saying plainly that the type is already sound, and its optional text-wrap suggestion is harmless, but B's one edit is better justified and adds more value while staying minimal.
